answer_raw:
DigitalOcean does not currently offer a specific "AI-optimized" GPU Droplet for high-speed local inference, so the fastest option is to use their **Inference-as-a-Service** via the Gradient AI Platform [2].

For running a model locally on a Droplet, hardware-specific pricing for high-end GPU instances isn't in what I found, so you would need to check the DigitalOcean pricing page for their latest GPU-backed compute options.

Regarding your specific questions based on what I found:

**Fastest option** — Use DigitalOcean's **Inference-as-a-Service** (Gradient AI Platform). This provides access to models like DeepSeek and Qwen via an API endpoint [2]. Because this uses managed infrastructure rather than a single virtual machine, it is designed for the low-latency requirements of LLM workloads [4].

**Cheapest option for a 7B model** — You would need to select a Droplet with enough RAM to hold a 7B parameter model (typically 8GB–16GB+ depending on quantization) and check the current cost of those specific resource tiers. The absolute cheapest Droplets start at **$4/month** [1][7][8], but a 2 GiB Droplet at **$12/month** is the standard for small production apps [1] and would likely be too small to run a 7B model locally [1]. 

If you choose to "Bring Your Own Model" (BYOM) to their managed service, you would pay **$5.00 per month** for storing the model weights in a service-managed location [6].
